# PR 264 performance review — round 1

Verdict: PASS-WITH-NOTES. No blocking performance finding at f808581187bf33c0513a637304264e9e4029ecb3. The post-deploy measurement is still owed at the live proof; the baseline below is the current fleet, not the PR binary.

Scope and basis
- Detached review worktree /Users/jordanknight/pi-hacking/review-264-f808581; git rev-parse HEAD returned the requested full SHA.
- Read AGENTS.md including resource cost and nice/shared-build rules. Read-only source review and live measurement only: no cargo, shared-build, tests, daemon restart or pane input. CI-green and private-daemon feature proofs are the request/PR author's evidence, not locally rerun proof.

Cost review (source-derived / inferential)
- Spawn registration wait: existing 50 ms sleep, at most about 20 iterations/s per outstanding waiting spawn, default deadline 30 s; no new resident loop or per-registered-seat work. crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1743-1779,1934-1954.
- Detection reuses that iteration's ONE capture. capture(pane,u32::MAX) does NOT request scrollback: crates/tmux/src/lib.rs:1102-1111 still sends exactly capture-pane -p -t <pane>, then trims locally. The previous 20-row call already fetched the same visible screen. There is no added tmux command, history scan or launch. New parsing/tail work is linear in visible screen bytes/rows per waiting spawn; temporary screen/row storage is released each iteration. Unsupported harnesses return before the trust parser allocates its rows (trust.rs:113-115).
- Opt-in --trust-folder: one send-keys attempt at most per second PER opted-in active wait, only while a matching prompt is visible. trust_key_at is set before awaiting the send, and the next tick must observe elapsed >= 1 s. No flag, no matching prompt, or no visible highlighted option sends no key; a key error exits. See http/mod.rs:1769-1824. This is a request-scoped cost of <= N launches/s for N simultaneous opted-in prompted waits, zero added launches/s once those waits end. Enter/Up/Down are fixed MenuKeys.
- Every such write uses TmuxAdapter::press_key -> existing run("send-keys",...) (tmux/src/lib.rs:1094-1099). run records tmux.send-keys before launch and uses pij_core::program::launch to resolve/cache an absolute executable (338-344). cheap_return only renames the old Enter method to MenuKey::Enter; its scheduling/rate does not change.
- spawn_sites.rs:17-27,179-243 scans core/daemon/harnesses/tmux and the other daemon crates; its known run builder site remains the launch point. The PR adds a caller of this already-counted launch path, not an uninstrumented Command builder. No local execution of this Rust sensor was claimed.
- F216: one POST /v1/close per tool call, no retry/poll added; existing daemon close guard/lifecycle work followed by at most one extension killPane call, using only data.kill_pane. The Rust close route reuses ONE pane_now result for both the note and kill_pane (lifecycle.rs:622-624), not a second tmux/liveness/roster check. Existing pane_now includes a roster scan, so this is request-time work that can scale with roster history, not a new periodic tax. The extension kill uses its existing one-shot tmux adapter; no new daemon launch site or persistent state is introduced.

Machine-wide launches include concurrent unrelated fleet work and this read-only sampling, not just the daemon. Per-parent sampling is a lower bound; the exact daemon counters independently stayed flat.
A contemporaneous subsequent pij-rs --json list reported 136 listed seats (55 Claude, 74 Copilot, 7 OMP), 0 unavailable; it was not an atomic census at the sample's start.

Note owed / handback
At the authorized live proof after deployment, repeat the same paired ping counters, spawn-rate 20 s and daemon CPU/RSS readings, retaining pid and commit; exercise an opted-in folder-trust spawn and confirm tmux.send-keys increments no faster than 1/s per such wait and stops once the prompt/wait ends. This round establishes baseline plus source-derived cost, not a measured PR-before/after improvement. Whole-machine rate is currently high even while the fleet daemon launches zero children; do not attribute that baseline to PR 264.

Harness feedback
Captured MW-001 through harness observe in .harness/temp/pij-united-dragonfly/session-buffer.md: a read-only cost-snapshot recipe should produce a timestamped JSON receipt joining daemon revision/pid, per-op deltas, machine spawn-rate and CPU-time/RSS, avoiding repeated manual joins. No tracked review-worktree file was changed.
